paragraphs.zh: The U.S. patent, US5424481 describes a process for preparation of methyl sulfonyl benzoic acids comprising oxidizing the corresponding methylsulfonyl toluenes with nitric acid and sulfuric acid in the presence of vanadium or cobalt compounds. In particular, oxidation of 2-nitro-4-methylsulphonyl toluene (NMST) is carried out in the presence of sulfuric acid and nitric acid using vanadium pentoxide as a catalyst to obtain 2-nitro-4-methylsulfonyl benzoic acid (NMSBA).
paragraphs.en: The U.S. patent, US5424481 describes a process for preparation of methyl sulfonyl benzoic acids comprising oxidizing the corresponding methylsulfonyl toluenes with nitric acid and sulfuric acid in the presence of vanadium or cobalt compounds. In particular, oxidation of 2-nitro-4-methylsulphonyl toluene (NMST) is carried out in the presence of sulfuric acid and nitric acid using vanadium pentoxide as a catalyst to obtain 2-nitro-4-methylsulfonyl benzoic acid (NMSBA).
paragraphs.notes: Marker printed as exactly three digits, [007], read at 8x; it is not zero-padded and there is no fourth digit. Cited document number read character by character at 12x: U, S, 5, 4, 2, 4, 4, 8, 1, that is seven digits after the US and no A or B kind code. The line is justified and the gap between the 8 and the final 1 is stretched wider than normal letter spacing, but it is clearly narrower than the word space before 'describes', so it is justification kerning and not a printed space; transcribed closed up as US5424481. Justification also squeezes two word spaces almost shut, in 'corresponding methylsulfonyl' and in 'sulfuric acid in the presence'; both are real spaces, kept as single spaces. Both spellings of the moiety appear inside this one paragraph and neither was normalised, per brief section 8: 'methylsulfonyl toluenes' and '2-nitro-4-methylsulfonyl benzoic acid' with an f, and '2-nitro-4-methylsulphonyl toluene' with a ph. A third form also appears, 'methyl sulfonyl benzoic acids' with a space between methyl and sulfonyl, which the brief does not list; it is what the page prints on its first and second lines and is kept. Note the asymmetry kept verbatim: the general sentence says 'nitric acid and sulfuric acid' and the NMST sentence reverses it to 'sulfuric acid and nitric acid'. Left margin line number 5 falls beside the fourth line of this paragraph and is excluded as furniture. Paragraph opens a fresh sentence, so it is not a continuation of p03, and it ends on a full stop, so it does not run onto the next drawing.

paragraphs.zh: The Chinese patent application, CN105669504A discloses a process for the preparation of 2-nitro-4-methylsulfonylbenzoic acid (NMSBA) by oxidation of 2-nitro-4-methylsulfonyltoluene (NMST). Specifically, the oxidation of NMST is carried out in presence of sulphuric acid and nitric acid using vanadium pentoxide as a catalyst.
paragraphs.en: The Chinese patent application, CN105669504A discloses a process for the preparation of 2-nitro-4-methylsulfonylbenzoic acid (NMSBA) by oxidation of 2-nitro-4-methylsulfonyltoluene (NMST). Specifically, the oxidation of NMST is carried out in presence of sulphuric acid and nitric acid using vanadium pentoxide as a catalyst.
paragraphs.notes: Marker printed as exactly three digits, [008], read at 8x; not zero-padded. Cited document number read character by character at 8x: C, N, 1, 0, 5, 6, 6, 9, 5, 0, 4, A, that is nine digits between the CN and the A. This paragraph is the last text on the page and it ends on a full stop, so nothing is cut off at the foot; the drawing below it is the last inked thing on the page. Printing oddity kept verbatim and not repaired: 'carried out in presence of sulphuric acid', with no 'the' before 'presence'. This paragraph spells the moiety with an f throughout and closed up with no space, '2-nitro-4-methylsulfonylbenzoic acid' and '2-nitro-4-methylsulfonyltoluene', which is a third and fourth form beyond the two the brief lists, while its 'sulphuric acid' takes the ph that the preceding paragraph gives as 'sulfuric acid' for the same reagent. Nothing normalised. Left margin line number 10 falls beside the second line and is excluded as furniture.

drawings.notes: First drawing on the page, printed above [007] with no text of any kind above it, so the paragraph it illustrates is not on this page: it belongs to the paragraph that ends on p03. between_markers therefore carries null for the opening bracket rather than a guessed number, per brief section 2 and 2a. Printed labels recorded per brief section 8: 'NMST' centred under the left structure, 'NMSBA' centred under the right structure. No formula number is printed anywhere in this drawing. Ink on this drawing is badly degraded, the condition the brief describes in section 9: every bond and every atom label is broken dotted ink and the two captions are bold and partly filled in. The arrow shaft is likewise broken ink and LOOKS dashed at page scale, but at 3x with autocontrast it is a single degraded solid shaft ending in one solid filled arrowhead pointing right, so arrow_style is solid and not dashed. Nothing is written below this arrow; reagents_below is empty because the page is empty there, not because it could not be read. Substituent positions were read off the drawing at 4x with autocontrast and not inferred from the names: both hexagons are drawn point-up, the C1 substituent hangs off the top vertex (CH3 on the left, the carboxyl carbon on the right), NO2 hangs off the upper-right vertex which is therefore C2, and SO2 off the bottom vertex which is therefore C4, with the S-methyl drawn down and to the left as H3C. Structure confidence is medium on both, for the broken ink alone; the connectivity itself resolved completely and the SMILES are given because every atom and bond was read, not assumed. presented_as is prior_art: the drawing sits in the BACKGROUND region of the document and is somebody else's route. Per brief section 8a that value describes how the page presents the drawing and not what the compounds are: NMST and NMSBA are in fact intermediates on the invention's own route later in the document, and intermediate_structure was not used here.

Second drawing, printed between [007] and [008] and illustrating the cited US5424481 process described in [007] immediately above it. Printed labels per brief section 8: 'NMST' centred under the left structure, 'NMSBA' centred under the right structure. No formula number printed. Ink on this drawing is clean and solid, unlike the first drawing on the page, and the arrow is a single solid shaft with one solid filled arrowhead pointing right. Above and below the arrow are kept separate per prompt rule 6. The three lines above the shaft are transcribed exactly as printed, including the trailing slash at the end of the first line: 'Sulphuric Acid/' and 'Nitric acid' are one slash-joined item broken across two printed lines, so a consumer that wants the reagent should read them as 'Sulphuric Acid/Nitric acid'; they are recorded as two entries because the page sets them on two lines and merging them would lose that. 'Vanadium Pentoxide' is the third line above the shaft. Below the shaft the page prints 145 followed by a degree ring and a capital C, with a space between the number and the degree ring; recorded here as printed with the degree character. DISAGREEMENT OF CONVENTION, recorded rather than resolved: p05.json, already written for this same run, renders the same kind of value in ASCII as '140-150 degC'. Both forms are now on disk for this patent and a downstream pass must expect either. Substituent positions read off the drawing at 4x, not inferred: both hexagons point-up, C1 substituent off the top vertex, NO2 off the upper-right vertex, SO2 off the bottom vertex with H3C down and to the left. Kekule pattern is an ordinary benzene in both. presented_as is prior_art and, unlike brief section 8a's definitional case, this one is prior art in the plain sense too: it is the route of the third-party US patent named in [007]. The value still describes the page's presentation, not the chemical role of NMST and NMSBA, which are intermediates of the invention later in the document.

drawings.notes: Third drawing, printed below [008] and illustrating the cited CN105669504A process described in [008] immediately above it. It is the last inked thing on the page; the whole band below it is blank. between_markers carries null for the closing bracket because no further paragraph marker appears on this page, and per brief section 2 the number it would have had on p05 was not guessed. Printed labels per brief section 8: 'NMST' under the left structure, 'NMSBA' under the right structure; in this drawing the two captions sit on roughly the same baseline as the H3C atom labels rather than clear below them, but they are set in the serif body face while the atom labels are sans serif, so they are typeset captions and not part of the graphic. No formula number printed. Clean solid ink, single solid shaft, one solid filled arrowhead pointing right. Above the shaft, three lines exactly as printed: 'Sulphuric Acid/', 'Nitric acid/O2', 'Vanadium Pentoxide'. As in the second drawing the trailing slash on the first line joins it to the second, giving 'Sulphuric Acid/Nitric acid/O2'; the subscript 2 of O2 is printed as a true subscript and is transcribed inline. Below the shaft the page prints 140-150 then a degree ring then a capital C with NO space before the degree ring, which differs from the second drawing on this same page, where 145 and the degree ring are separated by a space. Both kept as printed. Substituent positions read off the drawing at 3x, not inferred, and identical in layout to the other two drawings: C1 off the top vertex, NO2 off the upper-right vertex, SO2 off the bottom vertex with H3C down and to the left. presented_as is prior_art in both senses, as for the second drawing.

discrepancies.what: The scheme for the cited US patent drops the cobalt option that the prose beside it offers.
discrepancies.drawing_says: The second drawing names one catalyst only, Vanadium Pentoxide, above the arrow. No cobalt compound appears anywhere in it.
discrepancies.text_says: [007] says the US5424481 process oxidises 'in the presence of vanadium or cobalt compounds', naming cobalt as an alternative catalyst on equal footing with vanadium.

discrepancies.what: The scheme for the cited US patent carries a reaction temperature the prose does not state.
discrepancies.drawing_says: 145 followed by a degree ring and a capital C, printed below the arrow shaft.
discrepancies.text_says: [007] gives reagents and catalyst but states no temperature, and no temperature appears anywhere in the prose on this page.

discrepancies.what: The scheme for the cited Chinese application adds an oxidant the prose does not mention.
discrepancies.drawing_says: The third drawing prints 'Nitric acid/O2' above the arrow, bringing molecular oxygen into the reagent list.
discrepancies.text_says: [008] names only sulphuric acid, nitric acid and vanadium pentoxide as catalyst. Oxygen is not mentioned in [008] or anywhere else on this page.

discrepancies.what: The scheme for the cited Chinese application carries a temperature range the prose does not state.
discrepancies.drawing_says: 140-150 followed by a degree ring and a capital C, printed below the arrow shaft.

discrepancies.what: The first drawing on the page has no prose on this page to check it against, and its reagents are unlike those of the other two drawings.
discrepancies.drawing_says: Acetic acid, Sodium acetate and Cobalt (II) acetate tetrahydrate, three lines above the arrow, converting NMST to NMSBA. No mineral acid, no vanadium, no temperature.
discrepancies.text_says: Nothing. The drawing is printed above [007] with no text above it on this page, so the paragraph that introduces it is on p03 and the cross-check of prompt rule 10 cannot be run here. Recorded so a later pass joins it to p03 rather than to [007].

discrepancies.what: The same reagent is spelled with a ph and with an f on this one page, in the drawings and in the prose, and the two prose paragraphs disagree with each other.
discrepancies.drawing_says: Both clean drawings print 'Sulphuric Acid/' with a ph.
discrepancies.text_says: [007] prints 'sulfuric acid' with an f, twice, for the same reagent in the same reaction. [008] prints 'sulphuric acid' with a ph, agreeing with the drawings and not with [007]. Nothing normalised, per brief section 8.

discrepancies.what: The moiety name takes three different forms inside [007] alone, one of which the brief does not list.
discrepancies.drawing_says: The drawings spell nothing out; they use only the abbreviations NMST and NMSBA and the atom labels CH3, NO2, SO2, H3C, OH, O.
discrepancies.text_says: [007] prints 'methyl sulfonyl benzoic acids' with a space, 'methylsulfonyl toluenes' closed up with an f, and '2-nitro-4-methylsulphonyl toluene' with a ph, then '2-nitro-4-methylsulfonyl benzoic acid' with an f. The brief's section 8 lists only the two space-separated forms. The space-separated 'methyl sulfonyl' form is additional and is kept as printed.
